## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Tebhūmakakusala* is a textual section within the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, the first book of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The title refers to wholesome consciousness or meritorious thoughts leading to or pertaining to the three grades of existence across the respective spheres of sensual, fine-material, and immaterial realms [Kyaw Khine 1999]. In the commentary to the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, the *Atthasālinī*, wholesome factors operating across these three realms of existence (*tebhūmaka-kusalāni*) are explicitly contrasted with transcendental or supramundane path factors (*lokuttarāni*), particularly regarding the temporal dynamics between volition and the fruition of karmic results [Devdas 2004].
SuttaCentral lists no external parallels for the section and records two modern translations in two languages [SuttaCentral]. According to DharmaNexus, the text shares 1,061 matching passages with 27 other Pali texts, demonstrating substantial internal text reuse [DharmaNexus]. The closest alignments occur with adjacent and thematic sections of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, including *Rūpāvacarakusala* (Ds 2.1.2), *Abyākatavipāka* (Ds 2.1.7), *Arūpāvacarakusala* (Ds 2.1.3), *Lokuttarakusala* (Ds 2.1.5), and *Kāmāvacarakusala* (Ds 2.1.1) [DharmaNexus]. Substantial shared segments are also found across treatises of the *Vibhaṅga*, such as the *Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅga* (Vb 6), *Paṭisambhidāvibhaṅga* (Vb 15), *Sikkhāpadavibhaṅga* (Vb 14), and *Jhānavibhaṅga* (Vb 12), as well as the *Navakanipāta* of the Aṅguttara Nikāya (AN 9) and post-canonical Abhidhamma compendia including the *Abhidhammāvatāra* [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language matches with score 10 or higher are reported [DharmaNexus].
